Rashi on Chullin 34a:10:1.hebrew: וא"ל - ר"א: אי ממשקה ילפינן, תחלה נמי בעית למיעבדיה להאי אדם, כי היכי דמשקה נעשה ראשון. ורבי יהושע לא יליף מן המשקה, דהתם חומרי דמשקין הוא שעלולין לקבל טומאה, אבל מן האוכל יליף:
Rashi on Chullin 34a:10:1.english: And he said to him - Rabbi Eliezer [says]: If we derive this from liquid, then you would also have to make this person a rishon (first-degree [of impurity]), just as the liquid becomes a rishon. But Rabbi Yehoshua does not derive it from liquid, because there [with liquids] it is a stringency of liquids that they are prone to contract impurity, but from food he does derive it.

Rashi on Chullin 34a:10:2.hebrew: חוץ מן הטבול יום - דאיקלשא טומאה מיניה, ואע"ג דפסיל תרומה לא עביד משקה ראשון:
Rashi on Chullin 34a:10:2.english: Except for a tevul yom (one who immersed that day but awaits nightfall) - Because his impurity has been diminished; and even though he disqualifies terumah, he does not render a liquid a rishon (first degree of impurity).

Rashi on Chullin 34a:12:1.english: I too did not say [this] - [I meant that] one who eats food that has third-degree [impurity] status becomes [himself] a source of second-degree [impurity].

Rashi on Chullin 34a:12:2.english: Rather - With food that has teruma status, meaning chullin that was prepared in accordance with the purity level of teruma, as Rabbi Yehoshua stated explicitly above; and since it was prepared in accordance with the purity level of teruma, they treat it as fit to be eaten with a second-degree [ritual impurity].

Rashi on Chullin 34a:12:3.hebrew: מפני שטהרתה של תרומה טומאה היא אצל הקדש - כדאמרינן בחומר בקדש (חגיגה דף יח:): בגדי אוכלי תרומה מדרס לקדש. אלמא אין שמירת תרומה חשיבא שמירה אצל הקדש, דהא מדרסות לגבי תרומה מטמאין ואפילו בחולין, דהא טומאה דאורייתא היא, והאוכל תרומה נשמר הוא מן המדרס, ואפ"ה לגבי קדש לא חשיבא שמירה, וחיישינן שמא ישבה עליהן אשתו נדה. ה"נ שלישי דתרומה לגבי קדש מספקינן ליה בשני, הלכך האוכל שני לקדש, שמצינו שני עושה שני ע"י משקין. מדקאמר רבה בר בר חנה דאותביה ר"א לרבי יהושע 'שלישי שני למה', ואמר 'אף אני לא אמרתי' כו', ש"מ דהא דקתני במילתיה דרבי יהושע 'בחולין שנעשו על טהרת תרומה' ה"ק: באלו חולין יש שלישי בנעשו על טהרת תרומה, ועלה קאמר 'אף אני לא אמרתי', דדוקא קאמר ולא רבותא. דאי טעמא יהיב למילתיה, ואמר באיזו חולין הוא נעשה שני לקדש, בחולין שנעשו על טהרת תרומה, ומשום דטהרתה טומאה היא אצל הקדש, ולעולם שלישי בחולין שנעשו על טהרת הקדש איכא, מאי קא מותיב ליה ר"א 'שלישי שני למה', הא אשמועינן רבי יהושע טעמיה. ועולא דאמר לעיל דרבי יהושע בחולין שנעשו על טהרת הקדש נמי אית ליה שלישי, סבר דהא דקתני במילתיה דרבי יהושע 'בחולין שנעשו על טהרת תרומה' טעמא הוא דיהיב למילתיה, דבחולין דטהרת תרומה הוא דאמרינן נעשה גופו שני לקדש, משום דטהרתה טומאה היא אצל הקדש, אבל לא בחולין דטהרת הקדש. ולעולם אשמועינן דיש שלישי בנעשין על טהרת תרומה, וכ"ש בנעשין על טהרת הקדש. והאי מהדרי ליה לא שמיע ליה, דאינו לא במשנה ולא בברייתא מה שהשיבו זה לזה, אלא רבה בר בר חנה שמיע ליה מרביה. א"נ ס"ל לעולא דהאי 'אף אני לא אמרתי' לא היו דברים מעולם, דלרבי יהושע בתרוייהו קאמר דנעשה גופו שני לקדש, וטעמא משום דטהרת שניהם, בין נעשין על טהרת תרומה ובין בנעשין על טהרת הקדש, טומאה היא אצל הקדש. והאי דקתני לעיל 'בחולין שנעשו על טהרת תרומה' רבותא אשמועינן, דאפילו בהני איכא שלישי:
Rashi on Chullin 34a:12:3.english: Because the purity of terumah is [considered] impurity with respect to consecrated food - As we say regarding the stringency of consecrated food (Chagigah 18b): the garments of those who eat terumah have the status of midras [impurity] for consecrated food. This shows that the care taken for terumah's sake is not considered adequate care for consecrated food's sake, since midras-objects impart impurity to terumah - and even to ordinary food (chullin), because it is a Torah-level impurity - and one who eats terumah is indeed careful to avoid midras; nevertheless, with respect to consecrated food this is not considered adequate care, and we suspect that perhaps his wife, a menstruant, sat upon them [the garments]. So too here: a third-degree [impurity] of terumah is, with respect to consecrated food, treated with doubt as a second-degree; therefore the food becomes second-degree for consecrated food - since we find that a second-degree [impurity] produces [another] second-degree by means of liquids. From the fact that Rabbah bar bar Chana said that Rabbi Eliezer challenged Rabbi Yehoshua, "Why should a third-degree be like a second-degree?", and he answered, "I too did not say [that]," etc., we learn that what is taught in Rabbi Yehoshua's statement, "chullin that were prepared according to the purity level of terumah," means this: among these chullin there is a third-degree [status] in [chullin] prepared according to the purity of terumah - and it was about this that he said, "I too did not say [otherwise]," meaning that he spoke precisely of this case alone, not merely to cite a novel example. For had he given a reason for his ruling and said, "In which chullin does it become second-degree for consecrated food? In chullin prepared according to the purity of terumah, because its purity is [treated as] impurity with respect to consecrated food" - while in fact a third-degree still exists in chullin prepared according to the purity of consecrated food itself - what would Rabbi Eliezer's challenge, "Why should a third-degree be like a second-degree?", accomplish? Rabbi Yehoshua would already have told us his reasoning! And Ulla, who said above that according to Rabbi Yehoshua chullin prepared according to the purity of consecrated food itself also has a third-degree [status], held that what is taught in Rabbi Yehoshua's statement, "chullin prepared according to the purity of terumah," is [merely] the reason he gave for his ruling: that specifically in chullin [prepared according to] the purity of terumah do we say that the food itself becomes second-degree for consecrated food, because its purity is [treated as] impurity with respect to consecrated food - but not in chullin [prepared according to] the purity of consecrated food itself. But in truth he was teaching us that there is a third-degree [status] in [chullin] prepared according to the purity of terumah, and all the more so in [chullin] prepared according to the purity of consecrated food. And this exchange [between Rabbi Eliezer and Rabbi Yehoshua] he had not heard, since what they answered each other is found neither in a mishnah nor in a baraita - rather, Rabbah bar bar Chana heard it from his teacher. Alternatively, Ulla held that this statement, "I too did not say [otherwise]," never occurred at all - for Rabbi Yehoshua said, regarding both cases, that the food itself becomes second-degree for consecrated food, the reason being that the purity of both - whether prepared according to the purity of terumah or prepared according to the purity of consecrated food - is [treated as] impurity with respect to consecrated food. And that which is taught above, "chullin prepared according to the purity of terumah," was teaching us a novel point: that even in these [more remote] cases there is a third-degree [status].

Rashi on Chullin 34a:1:1.hebrew: דקתני בשר - מתניתין בבשר חולין קאי, ובשלמא פירות חולין אדם מתפיסן בטהרת תרומה כדי שיהא רגיל להתנהג בטהרת תרומה, שאם תתחלף לו תרומה בחולין ויאכל תרומה בחזקת חולין יהא אוכלה בטהרה, אבל בשר ליתא בתרומה, ואין כהן מתפיס לבשר חולין טהרת תרומה, משום דלא מיחלפא ליה תרומה בבשר חולין שיבא לאוכלה כדרך החולין:
Rashi on Chullin 34a:1:1.english: That it teaches [about] meat - The mishna is referring to non-sacred [chulin] meat. Now, granted, with non-sacred produce a person accepts upon it the sanctity of terumah [i.e., treats it with the stringencies of terumah-purity], so that he becomes accustomed to conducting himself with terumah-purity - so that if terumah should become mixed up with his non-sacred produce and he eats terumah thinking it is non-sacred, he will be eating it in purity. But meat has no counterpart in terumah [there is no such thing as "meat of terumah"], and a kohen does not accept upon non-sacred meat the sanctity/purity of terumah, because he would never mistake terumah for non-sacred meat and come to eat it in the manner of non-sacred [food].

Rashi on Chullin 34a:2:1.hebrew: בשר בבשר מיחלף - לפיכך דרך אוכלי קדש לאכול בשר חולין אפי' של חיה בטהרת הקדש, שאם תתחלף לו בשר הקדש בה, שיהא אוכלה בטהרה:
Rashi on Chullin 34a:2:1.english: Meat can be confused with meat - Therefore it is the practice of those who eat consecrated food to eat non-consecrated meat, even of a non-domesticated (undomesticated kosher) animal, in the purity required for consecrated food, so that if the consecrated meat becomes mixed up with it, he will [still] be eating it in purity.

Rashi on Chullin 34a:2:2.english: Meat cannot be confused with produce - Terumah applies only to produce and is not exchanged for meat; therefore, it is not the practice of priests to impose upon their non-sacred meat the purity status of terumah.

Rashi on Chullin 34a:3:1.hebrew: אמר עולא חבריא אמרין - כדאמר במתני', דקתני שלישי בחולין שנעשו על טהרת הקדש קמיירי, ודלא כרבי יהושע. ואנא אמינא דרבי יהושע נמי ס"ל הכי, דחולין שנעשו על טהרת הקדש אית בהו שלישי, והאי דקאמר רבי יהושע בחולין שנעשו על טהרת תרומה, רבותא אשמועינן דאפ"ה אית בהו שלישי, וכ"ש חולין שנעשו על טהרת הקדש:
Rashi on Chullin 34a:3:1.english: Ulla said: The colleagues say - As it says in the mishna, which teaches about "third-degree" [impurity], it is speaking of chullin prepared according to the level of purity of consecrated food (hekdesh), and not in accordance with Rabbi Yehoshua. And I say that Rabbi Yehoshua also holds this way: that chullin prepared according to the purity of hekdesh assumes third-degree [impurity]. And the reason Rabbi Yehoshua stated [his ruling] about chullin prepared according to the purity of teruma is to teach us a novel point - that even so it assumes third-degree [impurity], and all the more so chullin prepared according to the purity of hekdesh.

Rashi on Chullin 34a:5:1.english: Who are the colleagues? - [Those] who hold that Rabbi Yehoshua meant specifically [the case of] non-sacred food that was prepared in the purity level of teruma.

Rashi on Chullin 34a:5:2.hebrew: מה אהדרי רבי אליעזר ורבי יהושע להדדי - מה השיבו זה לזה, איש על דברי חברו:
Rashi on Chullin 34a:5:2.english: What did Rabbi Eliezer and Rabbi Yehoshua answer each other - What did they respond to one another, each addressing the words of his fellow.

Rashi on Chullin 34a:6:1.hebrew: מצינו שהאוכל חמור מן האוכל - האדם האוכל המאכל, חמור מן המאכל:
Rashi on Chullin 34a:6:1.english: We find that the eater is more stringent than the food - The person who eats the food is more stringent than the food [itself].

Rashi on Chullin 34a:6:2.english: How does the food not become like the food [that transmitted the impurity to it] - For [a food] that eats [i.e., comes into contact with] a first-degree-impure food should not thereby become first-degree itself [but only second-degree].

Rashi on Chullin 34a:7:1.hebrew: דחידוש הוא - שאין לו טומאה בגלוי, וכשהיא בבית הסתרים היא מטמאה האדם עד שהוא מטמא בגדיו, וכל שאר טומאות מטמאות בגלוי ואין מטמאות בבית הסתרים. הלכך גזרת הכתוב היא ואין למדין הימנה, ור"א סבר למדין:
Rashi on Chullin 34a:7:1.english: For it is a novelty - Because it has no impurity in the open, but when it is in a hidden place [i.e., in the throat] it renders a person impure to the extent that it renders his garments impure, whereas all other impurities render impure in the open and do not render impure in a hidden place. Therefore it is a scriptural decree, and one cannot derive [other laws] from it, whereas Rabbi Eliezer holds that one can derive [from it].

Rashi on Chullin 34a:7:2.hebrew: אלא מצינו שהמאכל חמור מן האוכלו דאילו המאכל - קיבל טומאה בכביצה, אוכלין טמאין שנגעו בו:
Rashi on Chullin 34a:7:2.english: Rather, we find that the food is more severe than the one who eats it, for the food - It contracts impurity, [when it is] the volume of an egg, from impure foods that touched it.

Rashi on Chullin 34a:7:3.hebrew: ואדם האוכל - אוכלין טמאין אינו טמא אא"כ אכל חצי פרס, כדתנן בעירובין (דף פב:), וחצי חציה לפסול את הגוייה, והן ב' ביצים:
Rashi on Chullin 34a:7:3.english: And a person who eats - One who eats impure foods does not become impure unless he eats half a peras, as we learned in Eruvin (page 82b), and half of that [amount] disqualifies the body [from eating teruma], and that is two eggs'-bulk.

Rashi on Chullin 34a:8:1.hebrew: טומאה משיעורין לא גמרינן - דשיעורין מילתא באנפי נפשיה היא, ולאו משום חומרא וקולא, אלא אוכל דמטמא בכביצה כך שיער בו הכתוב, "מכל האוכל אשר יאכל". ואמרינן בפ"ח דיומא (דף פ.): אוכל הנאכל בבת אחת ושיערו חכמים, אין בית הבליעה מחזיק יותר מביצת תרנגולת, ופסול גוייה בכחצי פרס. הכי תקון רבנן:
Rashi on Chullin 34a:8:1.english: We do not derive impurity from measures - For measures are a matter unto themselves, and it is not a matter of stringency and leniency. Rather, [regarding] food that renders impure with the volume of an egg, Scripture so measured it: "Of all the food which may be eaten" (Leviticus 11:34). And we say in the eighth chapter of Yoma (page 80a): [For] food that is eaten in one go, the Sages set a measure: the gullet can hold no more than the volume of a chicken's egg, and the disqualification of the body is at [the volume of] about half a peras. This is how the Rabbis instituted it.

Rashi on Chullin 34a:8:2.hebrew: ועוד לדבריך - שאתה למד טומאה משיעורין לעשות מאכל חמור מן האוכל, מה שאתה אומר "האוכל אוכל ראשון נעשה שני" - יפה אתה אומר, אלא: שני שני למה?
Rashi on Chullin 34a:8:2.english: And furthermore, according to your own reasoning - You derive the laws of impurity from the laws of minimum measures (shiurim), so as to make the [derivative] food more stringent than the [source] food itself. What you say - that food which touches food of the first degree becomes [impure in] the second degree - you say well; but why should [something that touches] a second-degree [item] also become [impure in] the second degree?

Rashi on Chullin 34a:9:1.english: He said to him: We find - [This refers to the fact] that food which is [ritually impure in] the second degree renders another [food] impure in the second degree.

Rashi on Chullin 34a:9:2.hebrew: ע"י משקין - אם נגע אוכל שני באוכל שהמשקה טופח עליו, נעשו משקין תחלה, כדקתני ואזיל: כל הפוסל את התרומה מטמא משקין להיות תחלה, וחזר המשקה ועשה האוכל שני. וכיון דאשכחן ע"י משקה דשני עושה שני, בשום דוכתא מחמרינן גבי אדם האוכלו למהוי כותיה, דאכילה חמירא ממגע:
Rashi on Chullin 34a:9:2.english: Via liquids - If a food of second-degree [impurity] touched a food that had liquid moist upon it, the liquid becomes a first-degree [impurity], as is taught further on: "Anything that disqualifies terumah renders liquids impure so that they become a first degree." The liquid then, in turn, renders the food a second degree. And since we find that through liquid a second-degree [item] can render [something else] a second degree, we are stringent in any such case regarding a person who eats it, that he should become like it [a second-degree impurity], for eating is more severe than touching.

Tosafot on Chullin 34a:10:1.hebrew: משקין תחלה נמי הוו כדתנן וכו' - לא בא להקשות שכמוהו יעשה האדם ראשון, דלמה יש לו להיות ראשון; אלא רצה לומר דהא דעביד שני, היינו דווקא ע"י משקין שהן תחלה. ול"ג מה שכתוב בספרים: אמר ליה רבי יהושע שאני משקין דעלולים לקבל טומאה, דמ"מ לא תירץ כלום:
Tosafot on Chullin 34a:10:1.english: Liquids are also a rishon (first-degree of impurity), as we learned, etc. - He [Rabbi Yehoshua] does not come to raise a difficulty that, like it [the liquid], the person should likewise become a rishon - for why should he be a rishon? Rather, he means to say that the fact that [the person] makes [something else into] a sheni (second-degree) is specifically by means of liquids, which are themselves a rishon. And we do not have the reading found in some texts: "Rabbi Yehoshua said to him: liquids are different, for they are prone to receive impurity" - for in any case, that does not answer anything.

Tosafot on Chullin 34a:12:1.hebrew: אף אני לא אמרתי כו' - י"מ, כי מהכא דייק דחבריא סברי דאין שלישי בחולין שנעשו על טהרת קדש, דהאי "אף אני לא אמרתי" היינו האי דקתני בברייתא בסוף מילתיה דרבי יהושע, בחולין שנעשו על טהרת תרומה; אבל בתחלה לא פירש רבי יהושע, עד ששאלו ר"א. ואם איתא דחולין שנעשו על טהרת קדש יש בהן שלישי, היה לו לפרש דלא מיירי בהו, כדי שלא יבא לטעות ולומר דאיירי בכל דבר שיש בו שלישי; אלא ודאי אין בו שלישי, ולכך לא הוצרך לפרש דאיירי בתרומה. ואע"ג דאיכא קדש עצמו שיש בו שלישי, סתמא דמלתא לאו בדידיה איירי, דאין דרך לאכול קדש שנטמא, ובני אדם בדילין ממנו:
Tosafot on Chullin 34a:12:1.english: I too did not say, etc. - Some explain (yesh mefarshim) that from here it is inferred that the colleagues (chavraya) hold that there is no third-degree [impurity] in chullin prepared according to the purity level of consecrated food (kodesh); for this [statement], "I too did not say [it]," refers to what is taught in the beraita at the end of Rabbi Yehoshua's statement - regarding chullin prepared according to the purity level of terumah. But initially Rabbi Yehoshua did not specify [this], until Rabbi Eliezer asked him. And if it were so that chullin prepared according to the purity level of kodesh has a third-degree [impurity] in it, he should have specified that he was not speaking about it, so that one would not come to err and say that he was speaking of anything that has a third-degree [impurity] in it; rather, [it must be that] certainly it has no third-degree [impurity], and therefore he did not need to specify that he was speaking about terumah. And even though there is kodesh itself, which has a third-degree [impurity], the plain sense of the matter is that he was not speaking about it, for it is not the way [of people] to eat kodesh that has become impure, and people keep away from it.

Tosafot on Chullin 34a:5:1.hebrew: מאן חבריא רבה בר בר חנה - לא ר"ל רבי אלעזר דלעיל, דלא הוה קרי ליה חבריא, דרבו הוה, כדאמר בפ"ק דב"ק (דף יא:) וביש נוחלין (ב"ב דף קכח.) דאמר עולא אמר רבי אלעזר הלכה גובין מן העבדים. אבל קשיא, אמאי לא קאמר עולא רבותי אומרים? ונראה דרבי אלעזר לא קאמר לעיל יותר, אלא הכא בחולין שנעשו על טהרת קדש עסקינן, והש"ס הוא דמסיים ודלא כרבי יהושע:
Tosafot on Chullin 34a:5:1.english: Who are "the colleagues"? Rabbah bar bar Chana - This does not mean Rabbi Elazar mentioned above, for he [Ulla] would not have referred to him as "colleagues," since he was his teacher, as it says in the first chapter of Bava Kamma (11b) and in [the chapter] Yesh Nochalin (Bava Batra 128a), that Ulla said in the name of Rabbi Elazar: the halakha is that they collect [debts] from slaves. But this is difficult: why did Ulla not say "my teachers say"? And it appears that Rabbi Elazar did not say anything more above [than what is cited there]; rather, here we are dealing with chullin that were made according to the purity level of consecrated food (taharat kodesh), and it is the Gemara itself that concludes that this is not in accordance with Rabbi Yehoshua.

Tosafot on Chullin 34a:7:1.hebrew: ואוכל עד דאכיל חצי פרס - אע"ג דמפרש ר"ת דבי"ח דבר גזרו על אדם האוכל כביצה שיהא טמא, מ"מ מייתי ראיה מפסול גוייה שהיה מתחלה בחצי פרס:
Tosafot on Chullin 34a:7:1.english: And he eats until he eats half a loaf (chatzi peras) - Even though Rabbeinu Tam explains that among the eighteen things [the Sages] decreed is that a person who eats [an impure food of] an egg's bulk becomes impure, nevertheless, [the Gemara] brings proof from the disqualification of the body, which was originally [measured] by [eating] half a loaf.

Tosafot on Chullin 34a:8:1.hebrew: טומאה משיעורין לא גמרינן - תימה, הרי מצינו נבלת בהמה דמטמאה ואוכלה טהור, אלמא מאכל חמור מן האוכל:
Tosafot on Chullin 34a:8:1.english: We do not derive [the laws of] impurity from [the laws of] measures - This is astonishing, for we find [that] an animal's carcass conveys impurity [to one who touches or carries it], yet one who eats it remains pure; this shows that the food [as a conveyor of impurity through contact] is more severe than [its impurity through] eating.

Tosafot on Chullin 34a:8:2.hebrew: שני שני למה - דאע"ג דאיכא למיגזר דבהדי דאכיל אוכלין טמאין שדי לפיו משקין דמעשר, מ"מ אי לאו דאשכחן בעלמא שני דעביד שני, לית לן למיגזר דלא להוו מילי דרבנן חוכא ואיטלולא:
Tosafot on Chullin 34a:8:2.english: Why [does] a second-degree [impurity make something] a second-degree? - For even though there is [room] to decree this - since while one eats impure foods, he puts liquids of tithe into his mouth [along with them] - nevertheless, were it not that we find elsewhere [an instance where] a second-degree makes [something] a second-degree, we would have no [reason] to decree this, so that the words of the Rabbis should not be a mockery and a laughingstock.

Tosafot on Chullin 34a:9:1.hebrew: מצינו שני עושה שני ע"י משקין - וא"ת: ואמאי לא קאמר ע"י ספר? דאמרינן בפ"ק דשבת (דף יד.) דהוי מי"ח דבר, וידים הבאות מחמת ספר נמי פוסלות תרומה, כדאמר התם. וי"ל: דלא בעי לאתויי אלא ממאכל דעביד מאכל אחר שני, דומיא דמאכל דעביד אדם שני; ועוד, דהא דספר עביד ידים שניות וגם פוסלות את התרומה, לאו משום טומאה אלא משום חומרא:
Tosafot on Chullin 34a:9:1.english: We find that a second [degree of impurity] makes [something else] a second, by means of liquids - And if you say: why did he not say [that we find this] by means of a scroll (sefer)? For we say in the first chapter of Shabbat (14a) that this is one of the eighteen decrees, and hands that come [to touch] on account of a scroll also disqualify terumah, as it says there. One can answer: he only wished to bring [proof] from a food that makes another food a second, similar to a food that makes a person a second; moreover, the fact that a scroll makes hands a second, and also disqualifies terumah, is not on account of [actual] impurity, but on account of a stringency.
